name: half-division-without-fast-math
rationale: DESIGN D279 (WP-FMX2, refining D253.2 and D253.12): what Metal's half division x / y rounds to, compiled without fast math, so the fdiv half carries no flag: once to half, a float quotient rounded to half, or x times a reciprocal rounded first. Each of 512 threads writes x / y and 1 / y, each half zero-extended to a word, dividing by its own load of y (both copies hold the same value); words 2 and 3 keep the 0xAB poison. Operands (x, y): 192 generic quotients with exponents in [-6, 6]; 96 pairs where the once-rounded half quotient, x times a reciprocal rounded to half, and x times a float reciprocal rounded to half differ; 64 half denormal numerators, divisors, or quotients; 32 quotients near or past the largest half; 32 special pairs (zeros, infinities, NaN, the largest half, denormals, equal operands, quotients 1/3); the rest over the whole range. The AIR has no loop.

name: a-view-of-a-larger-master-reads-the-smaller-ones-bytes
rationale: Views of two masters in one function (DESIGN D187 item 10): cover_two_up reads a through Swapped (byte 2, Wide's b) and writes a + 1000 through Wide (byte 0). Each view reaches its own master's bytes of the one cell, as large as Wide (measured on the M3 Max and an M4, probe ib1), so a becomes the authored b + 1000 (1000 to 1007.5, exact). Observes Wide's a plane.

name: a-view-of-a-smaller-master-writes-its-own-bytes
rationale: Views of two masters in one function (DESIGN D187 item 10): cover_two_down reads a through Wide (byte 0) and writes a + 100 through Swapped, whose a is byte 2, Wide's b. Each view reaches its own master's bytes of the one cell (measured on the M3 Max and an M4, probe ib1), so b becomes the authored a + 100 (100.5 to 115.5, exact). Observes Wide's b plane.

name: a-word-view-of-two-halves-moves-their-bits-a
rationale: Views of two masters whose members overlap (DESIGN D187 item 10): cover_two_word reads its first word through Word (w at byte 0: Wide's a in the low half, b in the high) and writes Wide's a as the high half's bits and Wide's w as the low half, so a becomes the authored b's bits and w the authored a's bits (zeros, subnormals, infinities and both signs among them, moved bit for bit). Each view reaches its own master's bytes of the one cell (measured on the M3 Max and an M4, probe ib1). Observes Wide's a plane.

name: a-word-view-of-two-halves-moves-their-bits-w
rationale: Views of two masters whose members overlap (DESIGN D187 item 10): cover_two_word reads its first word through Word (w at byte 0: Wide's a in the low half, b in the high) and writes Wide's a as the high half's bits and Wide's w as the low half, so a becomes the authored b's bits and w the authored a's bits (zeros, subnormals, infinities and both signs among them, moved bit for bit). Each view reaches its own master's bytes of the one cell (measured on the M3 Max and an M4, probe ib1). Observes Wide's w plane.

name: an-uncovered-sample-drops-its-imageblock-write-c
rationale: A fragment imageblock write beside a returned sample mask (DESIGN D187 item 10): cover_masked writes c = (x, y, 0.25, -1) and id = 4y + x + 100 and returns the mask 0, 1, 0xfffffffe or 0xffffffff by pixel class (x + 2y) % 4. Metal drops the fragment, and its imageblock write, where bit 0 is clear, so the pixels of classes 0 and 2 keep the cells the pass began with (the authored planes) and the others hold their own values (measured on the M3 Max and an M4, probe ib1). Observes the half4 c plane.

name: an-uncovered-sample-drops-its-imageblock-write-id
rationale: A fragment imageblock write beside a returned sample mask (DESIGN D187 item 10): cover_masked writes c = (x, y, 0.25, -1) and id = 4y + x + 100 and returns the mask 0, 1, 0xfffffffe or 0xffffffff by pixel class (x + 2y) % 4. Metal drops the fragment, and its imageblock write, where bit 0 is clear, so the pixels of classes 0 and 2 keep the cells the pass began with (the authored planes) and the others hold their own values (measured on the M3 Max and an M4, probe ib1). name: nan-model-loads-stores-and-selects-of-nan-halves
rationale: nan_moves on half: lane i loads halves a and b and a selector, and stores as half4: a, select(b, a, sel), its neighbour's a through threadgroup memory, and the selected element of half4(b, a, b, a). Lanes: each half NaN (quiet and signaling of either sign, payloads 0, 1, 2, 0xaa, 0x155, 0x1fe, 0x1ff) as a then as b, two distinct NaNs with either selector, and controls. Compiled without fast math; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bin
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element; the exact callback is loop-free and returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. The one-bin histogram parameters force every active scalar lane to bin zero, and the poisoned counter makes the bounded global-atomic write observable byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-three-rgb-lane-output

This entry splats the selected R, G, and B lanes into the complete poisoned 3x1 primary footprint byte-exactly.

name: a-dynamic-lane-of-an-eight-lane-vector
rationale:
A dynamic lane index into an EIGHT-lane vector. Vulkan's `OpVectorExtractDynamic` / `OpVectorInsertDynamic` only cover two-, three- and four-component vectors, so a wider one is emitted as an array and the dynamic lane is emulated: `emitter::body::core_inst::emit_large_vector_dynamic_extract` builds a chain of `OpIEqual` / `OpSelect` over every lane, and `emit_large_vector_dynamic_insert` does the same over eight `OpCompositeInsert` candidates. 93 corpus sources contain a dynamic `extractelement` on an `<8 x ...>` and not one authored case reached either function; measured with per-function coverage against every cased source, this fixture reaches both plus `dynamic_index_const`, and no cased source reaches any of the three.

The emulation is a select chain, so what has to be checked is that each lane's comparison selects the lane it names and that the fall-through default is lane 0. Every thread uses a different insert position (`tid & 7`) and a different extract position (`(tid * 5) & 7`, a full permutation because 5 is coprime with 8), so across the dispatch each of the eight arms of BOTH chains is the selected one exactly once. Four threads extract the lane they just inserted and four extract an untouched one, so a chain that selected the wrong operand of `OpSelect`, or that compared against the wrong lane constant, moves a specific word rather than all of them.

The `.ll` is hand-written and the `.metal` is a different spelling of the same computation: the module builds `<8 x i32>` in SSA and uses `insertelement`/`extractelement`, while the Metal source writes and reads a `thread uint v[8]`. Both start from the same eight constants (1, 11, 21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 71), write `tid + 1000` at the same position and read the same two positions; only the storage spelling differs. Simulating each independently gives (1000, 1000), (51, 1001), (1002, 1002), (71, 1003), (1004, 1004), (11, 1005), (1006, 1006), (31, 1007) -- so Metal matching is a check that the emulated chain agrees with a derivation it never ran. Every value is a small exact integer and the buffer starts all-zero, which no arm can produce.

`loop_free`: the eight-element initializer is written out rather than looped, so the module has no branch at all. One threadgroup of eight threads, one per lane.

name: the-rgb565-pack-at-the-exact-tie
rationale: `pack_float_to_unorm565` and `pack_half_to_unorm565` over sixteen lanes of buffer-supplied operands the Metal compiler cannot fold. Six of the words land on an EXACT tie: each component's f32 product with its field maximum is precisely k + 0.5 with k even, so rounding to nearest EVEN answers k and rounding ties away from zero answers k + 1, and every one of the three fields diverges at once. SPIR-V's Round leaves the tie direction to the implementation while RoundEven does not, and SPIRV-Cross spells the two as different MSL functions -- `round` and `rint` -- so the choice is observable. Ties on ODD k sit beside them as controls, since both rules answer k + 1 there; k = 30 and k = 62 put a tie at the top of the 5-bit and 6-bit fields, where rounding away would also be the only way to reach the field maximum. The half source cannot reach a discriminating tie at all -- the only half whose product with 31 or 63 is exactly k + 0.5 is 0.5 itself, and 15.5 and 31.5 round up under both rules -- so its sixteen lanes carry ordinary values and pin that the arithmetic happens at float width after the widen. The remaining float lanes hold the ends of the normalized range and values outside it that the clamp must bring back. The 33rd word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: cube-depth-and-comparison-gathers
rationale: The gathers D283 decodes (family B), in a kernel: lane i reads Lane i of buffer 0 (the 2D coordinate, comparison reference, and array layer; the cube direction) and writes nine float4s to out[9i .. 9i + 8] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB: the gathers of components x and w of texture 0 (cube rgba16_float 4x4) and of component z of texture 1 (cube array, 2 cubes), both of small integers; the gathers of texture 4 (depth32_float cube 4x4) and texture 5 (depth cube array, 2 cubes); and the comparison gathers (less_equal) of texture 2 (depth 2D 4x4), 3 (depth 2D array 4x4x2), 4, and 5, the reference the 2D texel itself on every third lane (a tie), else half or 1.5 times it. Every coordinate is a texel corner, so each footprint is four whole texels inside one face (the 2D corners (k + 1)/4, the cube face coordinates (k + 1)/4 on each of the six faces at |major axis| 1); distinct depths in (0, 1). 64 lanes. The AIR has no loop.

name: collapse-an-int3-range-to-its-outer-min-and-max
rationale: min=(10,12,11) and max=(20,21,23) give per-channel extents (10,9,12); min3 of those is 9 and max3 is 12, so 9*10 > 12 selects the rebalancing branch. There max3(min)=12 is not greater than min3(max)=20, so the shader collapses both bounds to scalars: min3(min)=10 and max3(max)=23, broadcast across xyz with w zero. Every one of the six min3/max3 calls is evaluated, and both the tonemapping and histogram sub-structs receive the same pair, so the poisoned 68-byte output is observed byte-exactly.

name: pi-scaled-sine-and-cosine-are-exact-at-every-half-integer
rationale:
sinpi and cospi are not sin(float(pi)*x) and cos(float(pi)*x), and this case is the device evidence for the argument reduction that replaced that pre-multiply. float(pi) is 3.1415927410125732, which sits 8.74e-08 above pi, so the scaled argument overshoots every zero crossing: the old lowering answered sinpi(1) as -8.74e-08 where Metal answers -0.0, cospi(100.5) as -1.03e-05 where Metal answers 0.0. Worse, the scaled argument is LARGE, and MSL's sin and cos flush to 0.0 above float(pi/2)*2^22, so cospi(1e7) came back 0.0 where Metal answers 1.0 -- a full-scale error, not a rounding one. Of the 64 lanes of this case's first version the old lowering got 29 wrong.

Both functions have period 2 and 2 is a power of two, so the reduction is exact and the anchors are exact with it. Every finite argument is a multiple of 0.5, where the reduced residue is exactly 0 and the answer must be an exact 0 or +-1; those lanes are the whole point. The two signed-zero conventions are measured, not assumed, and they are NOT the same for the two functions: sinpi returns -0.0 at every odd integer (1, 3, -1, -3) and +0.0 at every even one, while cospi returns +0.0 at every half-integer without exception, including 0.5, 2.5, -1.5, 10.5 and 100.5, whose quadrant arm is a negated sine and would otherwise be -0.0.

The large arguments are the second half of the case. 1e7, -1e7, 2^23, 2^24 and 1e20 are all past the point where every float is an even integer, so sinpi is 0 and cospi is 1 there, and the old lowering answered 0.0 for all five cosines. 10.5 and 100.5 are large enough for the scaled form to drift visibly but small enough to still carry a fraction. 8388607.5 and -8388607.5 (+-(2^23 - 0.5)) are the largest floats that still carry a fraction, so the reduction is exact at the top of the range.

The three non-finite arguments answer the canonical quiet NaN 0x7fc00000 for both functions, measured for +inf, -inf and NaN alike. The old lowering answered 0.0 for all six, because the reduction's x - x is a NaN and MSL's sin flushes a NaN to zero; the reduction now guards on |x| < inf and selects the NaN constant.

Arguments 15 to 21 are 4, -2, 4.5, -3.5, -10.5, 2^23 - 0.5 and -(2^23 - 0.5). In the case's first version they were 0.25, 0.75, -0.25, 1.25, 0.3, 0.7 and 1e-08, where the answer is an irrational number (pi times the argument, for 1e-08). MSL bounds sinpi and cospi at 4 ulp, and the lowering's arm off an axis is the device's sine or cosine, which Vulkan bounds at 2^-11 absolute, so those lanes read a device's rounding inside the bound, not an identity: lavapipe answered sinpi(0.25) and cospi(0.3) one ulp from Metal (DESIGN D204.4, D208). By Niven's theorem sinpi and cospi of a float are rational only at multiples of 0.5, where they are 0 or +-1, so every lane now asks an exact answer. The calls carry the default compile's fast flags, so MSL leaves the non-finite lanes and the zeros' signs undefined; the reduction answers them as Metal does (DESIGN D110.1, D204.2).

The 65th word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-one-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 21 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-three-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry writes the selected zero to both required poisoned output textures, with binding zero captured byte-exactly.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-half-16-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (offset 0, 64 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[k][n] (row stride w_ld = 16 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in half and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the half inputs.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply-half-16-non-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The non-transposed counterpart of the committed qmm_t_16_float case (DESIGN D272): qmm_n_16_half with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links three translation units, each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: vertex-float2-varying-passthrough
rationale: Three authored positions form a full-coverage triangle and constant float2 attributes traverse the declared varying; the typed observer captures its padded four-lane representation.

name: vertex-position-passthrough
rationale: Three authored float4 positions form a full-coverage triangle; the typed observer captures the passthrough position interface over the complete target.

name: ordered-not-equal-and-unordered-equal-at-nan-without-fast-math
rationale: DESIGN D279 (WP-FMX2, refining D253.2 and D253.12): Metal's fcmp one and fcmp ueq on float and half operands, compiled without fast math so a NaN operand is defined: one is false and ueq true when either operand is a NaN. Each of 64 threads writes four words, 1 or 0: one and ueq of its float pair (a, b), and of (half(a), half(b)). Pairs: a quiet NaN, a NaN with a payload, a signaling-pattern NaN, and a negative NaN against NaNs, finite values, zeros, and infinities, in both orders; equal values, both zeros in each sign order, infinities, and the largest float; distinct values; pairs equal only as half (within half's ulp) and pairs that both round past the largest half to the same infinity; the rest random finite pairs. No denormal operand. SPIRV-Cross renders OpFOrdNotEqual as MSL's !=, true for a NaN, so a translation of one as that opcode differs on MoltenVK at the NaN lanes. The AIR has no loop.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-multiple-passes-axes-min
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element along axis zero. Every four-lane reduction extent, per-thread count, per-threadgroup count, source and destination bound, broadcast extent, and NDArray size and stride is one, so all loops are bounded by the single authored element.

name: replay-a-chained-pointer-select-through-a-load-and-a-store
rationale: A pointer selected between two descriptors and then selected AGAIN against a third, so one select's arm is itself a selected pointer. Logical SPIR-V has no pointer value that can be any of three descriptors, so the emitter cannot merge them: it builds a SELECTED ACCESS TREE and replays every consumer once per leaf under the branch condition that selects it. Coverage, measured with llvm-cov over all 959 corpus-backed cased sources and all public fixtures: this one module reaches NINE functions no authored case or fixture reaches -- build_selected_access_tree and build_selected_access_arm in select_gep.rs, and emit_selected_access_tree_load, emit_selected_access_tree_load_value, emit_selected_access_arm_load_value, emit_selected_access_tree_store, emit_selected_access_tree_store_with_parent, emit_selected_access_arm_store and selected_access_branch_condition in raw_select.rs. That is the whole tree build plus both replay directions; select_gep.rs was 12 of 15 functions uncovered before this. The STORE row is what makes the replay observable. A store through a merged pointer is a read-modify-write on EVERY arm: the chosen descriptor gets the new value and each other descriptor gets its own bytes written back unchanged. Lane gid writes 500+gid into slot gid+8 of whichever buffer q names -- a slot no other lane touches, so there is no race -- and then reads slot gid+8 of all three buffers. Exactly one of the last three rows may show 500+gid on each lane and the other two must still hold their initial values, so an arm confusion moves a marker into the wrong row and a read-modify-write that writes a constant instead of the old value destroys the untouched ones. a holds 100+i, b holds 200+i, c holds 300+i; p is a on odd lanes and b on even, q is p on lanes 0-3 and c on lanes 4-7. Derived before running: out[0..7]=200 101 202 103 304 305 306 307; out[8..15]=201 101 201 101 301 301 301 301; out[16..23]=108 501 110 503 112 113 114 115; out[24..31]=500 209 502 211 212 213 214 215; out[32..39]=308 309 310 311 504 505 506 507. Every value is an exact small integer, so nothing depends on rounding.

name: multiply-add-contraction-flags-without-fast-math
rationale: DESIGN D279 (WP-FMX2, refining D253.2 and D253.12): which float and half multiply-add pairs Metal fuses when the module is compiled without fast math and an operation carries only the flags a #pragma clang fp grants. Each of 256 threads writes 11 float words (0-10) and 11 half words (16-26, zero-extended): a multiply and an addition with no flag (two statements), llvm.fmuladd (the control), a contract pair, a contract product used by two additions, c - a * b and a * b + c * d under contract, a reassoc pair, a reassoc contract pair, contract on the product only, and on the addition only. Operands as in multiply-add-contraction-shapes-under-fast-math: inexact products, addends cancelling the rounded product to within a few ulps on seven lanes in eight, and half double-rounding hazards on one lane in four of the single-product shapes. No NaN, infinity, or denormal. Words 11-15 and 27-31 keep the 0xAB poison. The AIR has no loop.
